incident-bot: ALERT: SLO burn-rate alert for service=text-gen-api, slo=99p_latency 30d. burn_rate_10m=4.9, burn_rate_30m=2.1, budget_remaining=0.42. paging: triggered. 

maya: ack — seeing the alert. looking at per-model tails now.

maya: dashboards: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/text-gen/tail-latency. spike started ~2025-03-15T12:03:00Z, correlated with a burst of long-context requests from a single client (client_id=acct-834).

jordan: any user-facing errors? i see increase in retries but 5xx rate is flat. most requests are just slow, not failed. :thinking_face:

maya: correct — increased queueing on older GPU pool, long kv-cache warmups. 95p and 99p latencies affected; p50 unchanged.

sam: paging noise context: our current burn alert pages on burn_rate_10m > 3x OR burn_rate_30m > 2x. that 10m sensitivity is causing pages for short bursts. propose multi-window policy instead: require either (a) sustained 30m burn > 2x OR (b) 10m burn > 5x AND absolute 99p latency > 2s to page. otherwise notify only.

anita: agree with reducing pager churn. can we also add an absolute error floor so tiny customers can't trigger infra-wide pages?

sam: yeah add absolute floor: page only if affected_tokens_per_min > 5000 or affected_request_rate > 10r/s.

jordan: customer impact summary: one high-volume customer had heavy long-context job that amplified tail latency. impacted some bulk ingestion jobs and a few webhooks timed out. no broad user outages. Customer-Success notified for the affected account.

maya: quick mitigation: shifted problematic traffic to dedicated burst queue, brough up an extra node in pool-rcu-3, and enabled kv-cache prewarm for heavy-models. latency improved in 8–10 minutes.

ops-bot: Pager suppressed: follow-up alert channel=#eng-oncall (notification only) due to auto-mitigation flag.

sam: for the post-incident tuning steps I propose: 
- update burn alert rule to multi-window described above
- add explanatory panel to text-gen dashboard showing burn_rate_5m/10m/30m + absolute affected_tokens metric
- create evaluation job to simulate long-context burst and verify no unwanted paging
- update playbook section 'slo-burn-page-criteria' with thresholds and examples

anita: i'll own the dashboard panel change. putting a quick draft on a PR.

maya: i'll open the incident ticket with timeline + mitigation steps and add customer impact notes.

jordan: i'll run the simulation in staging tomorrow and validate the new page rule. recommend thresholds: 10m>5 and 30m>2 for notify; paged only if (30m>2) OR (10m>5 AND absolute_99p>2000ms AND affected_tokens_min>5000).

sam: sounds good. also recommend we add a cooldown window: after a page, suppress new pages for 30m unless errors increase. reduces page storms during noisy flaps.

maya: ack. can someone update pagerduty escalation policy to reflect the cooldown?

anita: i'll add a note in PD config but want eng-sre approval before changing automated suppression.

jordan: handoff — i'm on call until 14:00 UTC. @sam will take over after that and oversee the alert rule rollout.

sam: taking over. tagging this as action-needed: update alert rule, dashboard, run sim, write postmortem.

maya: thanks team. TL;DR: short-lived tail spike from single customer caused SLO burn alert -> mitigated by routing + adding node; action items to tune multi-window paging, absolute floors, and cooldown.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: incident created (#INC-2025-0896). severity=sev2, owner=jordan.

anita: leaving a checklist in the incident ticket with PR links. will follow up when dashboard PR is ready.

sam: i'll land the alert change behind a feature flag and monitor for 24h before full rollout.

maya: if anything regresses ping me directly. otherwise i'll close the thread after postmortem draft uploaded. :white_check_mark:
